Multiparametric MRI Prostate | 10 Jan 2025 | Bravis Ziekenhuis Imaging

Clinical Indication:
Assessment of biochemical progression (PSA 8.1 ng/mL) alongside an abnormal digital rectal examination. Previous tissue sampling confirmed a positive result for ISUP GG 2.

FINDINGS:
Total gland volume registers at 39.35 mL. T2-weighted sequences highlight a subtle hypo-intense area in the left peripheral zone, spanning roughly 12 mm. Diffusion-weighted imaging shows mild restriction paired with an intermediate apparent diffusion coefficient. Dynamic contrast-enhanced phases lack early or focal enhancement. There is no evidence of extraprostatic extension or seminal vesicle invasion. Pelvic lymph nodes appear normal.

IMPRESSION:
PI-RADS 3 lesion identified in the left peripheral zone, measuring approximately 12 mm.
Prostate volume 39.35 mL.
PSAD 0.206 ng/mL/mL.
csPCa predicted probability 0.81509304

previous_notes.author: Dr. N. Kuiper (GP)
previous_notes.text: Clinical tracking shows the PSA climbing to 6.8 ng/mL, up from 4.6 ng/mL recorded in July 2023. Rectal palpation detected an asymmetric, firm nodule within the left lobe. Given the prior positive biopsy and current biochemical progression, the case was forwarded to urology for advanced imaging and tissue sampling.
